title: Beyond Physical Illness: Can Clinical Narratives Reveal Emerging Mental Health Risks in Chronically Ill Patients?
abstract: arXiv:2610.35761v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Mental-health risks such as depression, dementia, and suicidal ideation can emerge during hospitalization among chronically ill patients and may worsen without timely recognition and intervention. However, most existing mental health studies focus on patients with established psychiatric conditions rather than patients hospitalized primarily for physical illness. In this work, we investigate whether latent mental-health risk in chronically ill patients can be inferred from longitudinal clinical narratives. We construct a weakly supervised cohort around 4,000 patients from MIMIC-III using mental-health evidence extracted from discharge summaries. A hierarchical state-space framework derives mental-health representations from day-wise clinical narratives and models their temporal evolution for risk estimation throughout hospitalization. translated_title: 超越躯体疾病：临床叙述能否揭示慢性病患者中新出现的心理健康风险？
translated_abstract: 抑郁、痴呆和自杀意念等心理健康风险可能在慢性病患者住院期间出现，若未能及时识别和干预则可能恶化。然而，现有的大多数心理健康研究关注的是已确诊精神疾病的患者，而非主要因躯体疾病而住院的患者。在这项工作中，我们研究能否从纵向临床叙述文本中推断慢性病患者的潜在心理健康风险。我们利用从出院总结中提取的心理健康证据，基于MIMIC-III构建了一个包含约4,000名患者的弱监督队列。该层次化状态空间框架从每日临床叙述中推导心理健康表征，并对其时间演化进行建模，从而在整个住院期间进行风险估计。初步结果表明，使用所提出的表征能够改进二分类风险预测的效果。
tldr: 该研究提出一种层次化状态空间框架，从慢性病患者的每日临床叙述中建模心理健康状态的时间演化，从而在住院全程预测潜在心理健康风险。
en_tdlr: This study proposes a hierarchical state-space framework that models the temporal evolution of mental-health representations from day-wise clinical narratives of chronically ill patients, enabling risk estimation of latent mental-health issues throughout hospitalization.
